msvcrt.lib — Microsoft's /MD C runtime import+static library, as linked into game.dat
=====================================================================================

msvcrt.lib
  sha256  e888617fbd2e153645b92122deab1c6ec437905431243c43aa7310164c0e7779
  size    431,200 bytes
  from    Visual C++ 7.1 (Visual Studio .NET 2003), Vc7/lib/msvcrt.lib

A byte-identical copy of the file already committed under build/toolchains/
vs2003/ in the Open-BFME-1 submodule, which is the compiler this repo builds
every function with. It is copied here for the same two reasons comsupp.lib is:
ledger rows name a path without spaces, and progress.py routes them to the
vendored identity lane — this is Microsoft's compiled code, not the game's.

Why this library and not libcmt.lib
-----------------------------------
game.dat is a /MD build, so the bulk of the CRT lives in msvcr71.dll and never
appears in .text at all. msvcrt.lib is the half that does: an import library for
the DLL entry points PLUS the objects the linker always copies in regardless —
the 64-bit arithmetic helpers, the runtime-check (/RTC) support and the PDB
lookup it needs.

libcmt.lib and libc.lib are the static-CRT variants. Their members place too,
because most of these objects are compiled from the same sources, but they are
not what this binary links and they cost 2.9 MB and 2.6 MB. One body placed
from libcmt alone (__byteswap_ulong, 35 bytes at 0x006038EF); not worth
committing a 2.9 MB library for, and it is left unclaimed.

Region
------
Sixteen rows across fourteen archive members, all in the startup helper block at
RVA 0x00628FA4-0x00629A2A: the stack probe, the SEH and EH frame helpers, the
eh-vector iterators, type_info's deleting destructor, __ftol2 and the 64-bit
arithmetic helpers. The /RTC and PDB-lookup bodies are hand-written under
Code/Libraries/Source/CRT/, and they stay there: tools/conversion_gate.py refuses
to move a clean C++ row into an archive. stack.obj is not used: extracting
__RTC_CheckEsp from it also brought @_RTC_CheckStackVars@8, a duplicate of
CRT/RtcStack.cpp at the real link, so that row is Code/masm_dumps/RTC_CheckEsp.asm
by owner approval (2026-11-04). Each row names the member its bytes come from, and ./build.sh
extracts that member and byte-compares it against retail like any other row.

How the addresses were decided
------------------------------
Each member's COMDATs were carved, every relocation site masked, and .text
searched for what was left. ./build.sh then checks the whole row extent
against retail. Ghidra's function sizes are a second opinion, and they agree
for only eleven of the sixteen rows:

  11 rows   Ghidra size equals the row size (the arithmetic helpers,
            __SEH_prolog/__SEH_epilog, __ftol2, __chkstk, __EH_prolog).
   3 rows   Ghidra is shorter because it splits the inline __except filter
            or __finally block off the body: __ArrayUnwind (Ghidra 47 of 94),
            `eh vector destructor iterator' (72 of 96) and
            `eh vector constructor iterator' (74 of 98). The archive section
            proves the longer extent.
   2 rows   No Ghidra entry: `eh vector copy constructor iterator' (ehvccctr)
            and type_info's deleting destructor (ti_inst). The archive
            section's extent and the retail bytes are the only boundary
            evidence.

The first commit of this file held back ten further placements, seven where
Ghidra's size disagreed and three with no Ghidra entry and no int3 run in front.

Licence
-------
The file is committed as a build input for byte-verification only: it is read
to prove that retail bytes match Microsoft's shipped code, and none of it is
compiled into or redistributed as part of any binary this repo produces.
